description: When David asked 'What transcript are you using, it should be full not excerpts?', I concluded the full transcript was unrecoverable from Obsidian (checked only the one curated vault note, which is explicitly labeled as excerpts) and the plaud-transcripts staging directory (confirmed empty via Glob), then went to considerable effort to reconstruct the transcript via Claude-in-Chrome browser automation against the live Plaud web app, including repeated scroll/capture/dedupe cycles against a virtualized UI. David then corrected me: the full transcript was already sitting in Obsidian. I never ran a vault-wide search for other notes or an attached/linked full-transcript file before deciding a browser-scrape was necessary.
correction: Before concluding a source doesn't exist, search exhaustively across the actual store, not just the one file already open in context. For Obsidian specifically, that means running search_vault / search_vault_smart across the whole vault (not just re-reading the one known note) before ruling out that the full transcript is there, e.g. as a linked attachment, a sibling note, or in a different folder than the curated summary note.
systemic_fix: Before invoking any recovery workflow (browser automation, re-fetching from an external API, etc.) to reconstruct data that might already exist locally, run a full-vault/full-filesystem search first and treat that as a blocking prerequisite step, not an optional check. Update the plaud-transcripts skill and/or harper meeting-coaching workflow to include 'search_vault_smart across entire vault for full transcript before assuming excerpt-only' as an explicit pre-flight step.
